_note: State chain and traction rules for passenger vehicles, shown on pass pages. Each line paraphrases or quotes the linked official page only. Re-read the sources before each winter season; change 'checked' only after a re-read.

rules: When a pass shows “Chains required”, you must have chains or an approved alternative traction device on your drive tires to enter.
All-wheel-drive vehicles are exempt only with all wheels in gear and “equipped with approved traction devices”, and with chains for one set of drive tires carried in the vehicle.
Studded tires are legal November 1 to March 31, and they do not meet a posted chain requirement.
sources: WAC 204-24-050 (Washington State Patrol tire chain rule)

rules: R-1: chains required, except cars and light trucks under 6,000 lb with snow tires on at least two drive wheels. Those must carry chains.
R-2: chains or traction devices required, except four-wheel or all-wheel drive with snow-tread tires on all four wheels. Those must carry traction devices.
R-3: chains or traction devices on all vehicles, no exceptions.
With chains on, the speed limit is 25 or 30 mph. The CHP can cite drivers who don’t chain up when signs say so.
Where signs say to carry chains or traction tires, you must have them in or on your vehicle.
Vehicles rated 10,000 lb GVW or less and not towing may use traction tires instead of chains: studded tires, or tires marked with the mountain-snowflake symbol.
In very bad conditions all vehicles may be required to use chains.
Studded tires are legal November 1 to March 31. Ignoring chain or traction tire signs is a Class C traffic infraction.
Idaho’s chain-up law applies only to commercial vehicles over 26,000 lb; ITD says it “does not apply to most drivers on the road”.
Studded tires are legal October 1 to April 30.
sources: ITD: What you need to know about the chain up law
ITD: Studded tires are legal in Idaho from Oct. 1 to April 30

rules: Level 1 chain law (hazardous conditions): travel can be restricted to vehicles with tire chains, vehicles with adequate snow tires, or all-wheel-drive vehicles.
Level 2 (extremely hazardous): only vehicles with tire chains, or all-wheel-drive vehicles with adequate mud-and-snow or all-weather-rated tires.
Fines: $250 for violating the restriction; $750 if the violation causes a highway closure.
